title: Auto-Recycle Workflow Metric Critique
scenario: A pharmacy runs an auto-recycling workflow that retries rejected claims by correcting fields like quantity, day supply, or diagnosis code. The operations team proposes tracking 'total number of claims successfully recycled per week' as the key workflow health metric.
prompt: The operations team wants to measure auto-recycle workflow effectiveness with 'total number of claims successfully recycled per week'. What is wrong with this metric? Propose a better alternative.
instructions: One short sentence: name the flaw, propose a fix. Match PAA terseness (e.g., 'Should be normalized. Ride Cancellation Rate is better').
expected_themes: should be a rate not a count
reference_answer: Should be normalized per rejection. Recycle Success Rate (recycled claims / total rejections) is better.

grading_rubric.criterion: Identifies lack of normalization as the flaw
grading_rubric.description: Names that the metric is a count not normalized by rejection volume or total scripts

grading_rubric.criterion: Proposes a rate metric as the fix
grading_rubric.description: Suggests recycle success rate, acceptance rate after recycle, or similar rate metric
Delivers the critique and fix in one or two short sentences, not a paragraph

hints: Think about what happens if the pharmacy grows and total rejections double.
Compare a week with 100 recycled out of 200 rejections to a week with 200 recycled out of 500 rejections.
The metric should be a rate: successful recycles divided by total rejections.
common_mistakes: Proposing a different count metric instead of a rate (e.g., 'track number of rejections' instead of a success rate)
Writing a long paragraph instead of one sentence naming the flaw and fix
Focusing on downstream impact (like time saved) instead of the normalization flaw itself

_meta.scenario: a pharmacy auto-recycling workflow that retries rejected claims with corrected fields
